abstract: Research on plant viruses depends on taxonomy, nucleic acid sequences, host and disease records, molecular targets, and antiviral assays. These data are distributed across separate resources, making integrated retrieval and comparison difficult. PlantVirDisConDB (https://dpai.ccnu.edu.cn/PVDCDB) is freely accessible without login or registration and links these data through curated plant virus records. At the July 2026 reporting date, it comprised, in round numbers, 5000 virus and subviral agent records and 38 000 sequence accessions. It also included approximately1900 hosts, 9000 virus-host associations, 4800 disease names, 5000 structure records, and 25 000 small molecules. Direct assay records for plant viruses are distinguished from general antiviral background data; experimental and predicted structures, and measured activities and model outputs, are also labelled separately. Linked record pages support retrieval across these data types, access to individual sequence records, target searches, and molecular similarity searches. An activity prediction module ranks candidate molecule-virus pairs with applicability warnings and does not imply experimental or field efficacy. PlantVirDisConDB links viral nucleic acid entities to hosts, phenotypes, targets, and antiviral information and is updated through continuing curation and user feedback.
